gloss: upper level; upper tier; high position

definitions.gloss: upper level; upper tier; upper row
definitions.explanation: The upper section of something divided into levels, such as a shelf, display case, or seating area.
In martial arts (especially kendo), the stance where the sword or weapon is held high above the head, ready to strike downward.

examples.japanese: {上段|じょうだん}の{棚|たな}に{置|お}く。
examples.english: To put it on the upper shelf.

examples.japanese: {上段|じょうだん}の{席|せき}は{見晴|みは}らしがいい。
examples.english: The upper-level seats have a good view.

examples.japanese: {書類|しょるい}は{上段|じょうだん}の{引|ひ}き{出|だ}しに{入|い}れてあります。
examples.english: The documents are in the upper drawer.

examples.japanese: {上段|じょうだん}に{構|かま}える。
examples.english: To take a high guard stance.

examples.japanese: {上段|じょうだん}から{打|う}ち{込|こ}む。
examples.english: To strike from a high position.

examples.japanese: {相手|あいて}が{上段|じょうだん}に{構|かま}えたので、{中段|ちゅうだん}で{受|う}ける{準備|じゅんび}をした。
examples.english: When the opponent took a high stance, I prepared to receive in the middle guard.

notes:
Part of a three-level system used to describe vertical positions or martial arts stances. Not to be confused with the homophone {冗談|じょうだん} (joke).

THREE-LEVEL SYSTEM:
- {上段|じょうだん}: upper level
- {中段|ちゅうだん}: middle level
- {下段|げだん}: lower level

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {上段|じょうだん}の{棚|たな}: upper shelf
- {上段|じょうだん}に{構|かま}える: to take a high guard stance
- {上段|じょうだん}から{振|ふ}り{下|お}ろす: to swing down from a high position
- {上段|じょうだん}の{間|ま}: the upper chamber (in traditional architecture, the elevated section of a room for honored guests)
